about.title: About This Project
about.intro: A personal project built to practice production-grade frontend engineering in the open: typed tool registry, real tests, and no backend to hide behind.
whatParagraphs: Frontend Multitool is a growing collection of practical developer utilities such as formatters, encoders, generators, and converters that run entirely in the browser. There is no API layer processing your input.
The real point of the project is not only the tools themselves, but the codebase around them: a registry structure that keeps new tools linked, tested, and discoverable in a consistent way.

principles.title: Typed registry instead of page sprawl
principles.description: Each tool is a typed config object. A prebuild check blocks duplicate IDs, missing pages, or broken references before they can ship.

principles.title: Tests that verify real logic
principles.description: Vitest and Testing Library cover more than rendering: they verify color conversion, UUID decoding, validation behavior, and other real utility logic.

principles.title: Client-side by architecture
principles.description: No cookies, no tracking, no backend. The theme is resolved before first paint so the UI starts in the correct color scheme immediately.

about.lighthouseDescription: Measured against the production deployment, not the dev server. Update these after major changes instead of trusting them forever.
stackItems: Next.js 16 (App Router) for routing and page-level metadata
React 19 and TypeScript in strict mode with one shared tool type
Tailwind CSS 4 on top of a small set of theme variables
Vitest and Testing Library as a release-quality verification layer
Small internal CLI scripts for scaffolding and validating tools

sections.title: Your privacy matters
paragraphs: We take privacy seriously. The short version: we do not collect, store, or transmit the content you use in these tools.

sections.title: TL;DR
paragraphs: Your data stays on your device. All tools run locally in the browser. Privacy is part of the architecture, not an afterthought.

sections.title: How the tools work
paragraphs: All tools run entirely in your browser. In practice that means:
bullets: No accounts or personal details required.

sections.title: What we store
paragraphs: Very little, and only locally: currently preferences such as theme and language so the interface stays consistent on your next visit.

sections.title: Third parties and cookies
paragraphs: There are no integrated tracking services. Theme and language preferences are stored locally, not managed through advertising or analytics cookies.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: Because no content is sent to a backend, there is no server-side data store for us to secure. It still makes sense for you to keep your browser up to date, especially on shared devices.

sections.title: Open source and contact
paragraphs: The source code is open to inspection. If you have questions, you can open an issue in the repository.
